Case_24004/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Image 1: Ulcerated lesion of the chin, most advanced lesion at time of presentation

description.short_caption: Ulcerated lesion on the chin with central necrosis.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower face of an older individual, focusing on the chin. A single ulcerated lesion is visible on the midline of the chin. The lesion has a dark, necrotic center surrounded by erythematous and slightly raised borders. The surrounding skin appears wrinkled and aged, with no other visible lesions or abnormalities.

Case_24004/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Image 2: Lesion on nose of patient, stage prior to eschar formation

description.short_caption: Lesion on the nose prior to eschar formation.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a lesion on the dorsum of the nose. The lesion appears erythematous with a central area of ulceration or necrosis. The surrounding skin shows no significant swelling or discoloration. The lesion is in a stage prior to eschar formation, as no dark scab is visible.

Case_24004/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Image 3a: All Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain Periodic acid–Schiff–diastase stains of lung biopsy: round/oval yeast with narrowed-based buds

description.short_caption: Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain showing round/oval yeast forms with narrow-based budding.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image of lung tissue is stained using Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain, which highlights fungal elements. Numerous round to oval yeast forms are visible, with some showing narrow-based budding. The fungal elements appear darkly stained against a lighter background, consistent with the staining technique. The periodic acid–Schiff–diastase stain further enhances the visualization of fungal structures.
visible_findings: dark fungal elements highlighted by silver stain

Case_24004/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Image 4: Histopathology of lung with intracellular Emergomyces: round/oval yeast with narrowed-based buds.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of lung showing intracellular round/oval yeast forms with narrow-based budding.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates numerous intracellular and extracellular round to oval yeast forms, some of which exhibit narrow-based budding. The yeast forms are distributed within a background of inflammatory infiltrate and fibrotic tissue. The findings are consistent with a fungal infection, potentially caused by Emergomyces or a similar organism.

Case_24004/figure8.jpg.source_caption: Image 5: Emergomyces canandensis colonies grown on Potato Flake Agar. Colonies were slow growing, initially white with light red/brown and as they matured became white/tan with yellow and brown.

description.short_caption: Emergomyces colonies on Potato Flake Agar showing white, tan, and yellow-brown pigmentation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate containing colonies of a fungal organism grown on Potato Flake Agar. The colonies are circular and exhibit a range of colors, including white, tan, and yellow-brown. The colonies appear to be slow-growing, with a fluffy texture and a slightly raised morphology. The plate is labeled 'p11,' and the agar medium is light brown in color.

Case_24004/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Image 3b: All Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain Periodic acid–Schiff–diastase stains of lung biopsy: round/oval yeast with narrowed-based buds

description.short_caption: Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain of lung biopsy showing round/oval yeast with narrow-based budding.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lung biopsy stained with Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain. The stain highlights numerous round to oval yeast forms with narrow-based budding, appearing as black structures against a green background. The fungal organisms are distributed throughout the tissue, consistent with a fungal infection. The stain enhances the visualization of fungal cell walls, making the organisms prominent.

Case_24004/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Image 3c: All Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain Periodic acid–Schiff–diastase stains of lung biopsy: round/oval yeast with narrowed-based buds

description.short_caption: Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain of lung biopsy showing round/oval yeast forms with narrow-based budding.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of lung tissue stained with Grocott–Gömöri's methenamine silver stain. The stain highlights numerous round to oval yeast forms, which appear as black structures against a green background. Several of the yeast forms exhibit narrow-based budding. The surrounding tissue shows a fibrous and cellular matrix, consistent with lung parenchyma. This staining technique is commonly used to identify fungal organisms in tissue samples.
